requirements.title: Level-2 expressions are the numeric-operator layer over level-1 expressions
requirements.definition: Level-2 expressions are built from level-1 expressions and optional numeric operators in four distinct precedence steps: exponentiation, multiplication/division, unary plus/minus at the first add-op position, and binary plus/minus in the left-recursive level-2 chain. The grammar specifies right recursion for power and left recursion for multiplication and binary addition/subtraction.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_098.json reads all50 original base units and131 fine units of the 10.1.1 and 10.1.2 expression chain, derives the precedence structure independently from the grammar, and verifies all502 grammar heads. The derived chain is primary, then defined unary, then power, then multiply and divide, then unary plus and minus, then binary plus and minus, then concatenation, then a single relation, then NOT, AND, OR and finally EQV and NEQV, with defined binary operators lowest; the catalogue text matches that chain at that granularity. Five blocking findings were raised and closed before this record. Three replaced oracles that could not work: a literal value cannot observe the grouping of an associative operator, and an execution-path oracle cannot observe AND grouping because the standard does not require short-circuit evaluation. One moved a defined-binary rejection from R1023 syntax to the applicability and generic-resolution owners 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2. The fifth corrected the replacement text itself, which had claimed unobservability too broadly: grouping is unobservable only for intrinsic operands, while a non-associative defined extension of the same operator symbol makes it observable by value, and that route is now recorded as the concrete future shape. Expression interpretation, evaluation and constant expressions remain owned by 10.1.3 through 10.1.12 and intrinsic assignment by the registered 10.2.1.3. All facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
